claim: Core-lib wave-rollout mechanics, measured as a bun-vs-pnpm head-to-head. bun remains the recommended driver for its native mechanics (committed-bunfig frozen, package.json catalogs) and the 200-app/truly-cold install cases; against pnpm 12 (the Rust CLI) the full-re-resolve speed story is scale-dependent — bun ~6x faster at 200 apps, pnpm-hoisted faster at the measured 1,000- and 2,000-app points, the CI frozen container a near-tie (bench/install-bench.json; see speedContext). Determinism is the lockfile + a frozen install (the range is inert): bun fails closed on drift with one committed bunfig line (frozenLockfile=true); pnpm fails closed with --frozen-lockfile and auto-enables frozen in CI. Named catalogs route two cohorts to two versions in one lockfile and a repoint edits zero consumer manifests on both (bun in package.json, pnpm in pnpm-workspace.yaml). Both accept workspace: as a catalog value and link the local package (pnpm 12 lifted pnpm 10's ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_INVALID_WORKSPACE_SPEC rejection — parity). Both bake a CONCRETE range on publish (workspace:^ -> ^2.5.0), so advancing a universal lib is a republish-fanout. bun does not read pnpm-workspace.yaml catalogs, so author them in package.json.

speedContext.note: The install state matters and both directions are recorded (pnpm 12.8.1, the Rust CLI). COLD install (no lockfile, fresh node_modules, warm store): bun ~6x faster at 200 apps (0.14s vs pnpm-isolated 0.83s / pnpm-hoisted 0.81s); at scale the story INVERTS — pnpm-hoisted 1.4s vs bun 2.1s at 1,000 apps and 3.4s vs 8.7s at 2,000, where bun's cold is the slowest of the five measured configurations (measured ceiling 2,000 apps). TRULY-COLD (fresh store + metadata, network; single samples): bun 1.3s vs pnpm-hoisted 2.4s at 200 apps. WARM (lockfile + store, node_modules removed): pnpm-hoisted 0.9s at 1,000 / 1.4s at 2,000 vs bun 3.5s / 10.1s. bun wins the 200-app cold and truly-cold cases; the CI-runner frozen container install is a near-tie (bun 1.04s vs pnpm 1.08s fresh, 0.47s vs 0.54s cache-restored; bench/container-install-bench.json); pnpm 12 hoisted wins cold and warm at the measured 1,000- and 2,000-app points.

bun.config: bunfig.toml [install] frozenLockfile=true; bare bun install on drift
bun.diagnostic: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen
bun.sourceNote: frozen_lockfile is set only by --frozen-lockfile / `bun ci` / --production / bunfig (CommandLineArguments.zig:797, PackageManagerOptions.zig:335-344,613-620); env.isCI() only disables the progress bar (PackageManagerOptions.zig:392).

lockfilePortability.note: pnpm 12.8.1's launcher records the packageManager pin in pnpm-lock.yaml as a two-document YAML stream (packageManagerDependencies preamble document, measured present); with the pin removed a frozen install exits 1 (ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE) — keep the pin with the lockfile through a rollout.

pnpm.note: pnpm 12.8.1 accepts every workspace: form as a catalog value and links the local package (sentinel-proved) — parity with bun; pnpm 10 rejected every form with ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_INVALID_WORKSPACE_SPEC

publishBakesConcrete.implication: a consumer catalog cannot repoint a baked range inside a dependent lib's tarball; a universal lib re-exported through every other lib advances by republishing its dependents.
